memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before the LORD as a wave offering, as Moses commanded." - Lev 9:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The wave offering was visible worship. Aaron lifted the portions and moved them before the LORD, where the whole assembly could see.

Faith that stays entirely internal tends not to survive.

That is not a call to showiness — Jesus warned sharply against practising righteousness in front of others to be seen by them (Mtt 6:1). The difference is motive. Aaron waved the offering as an act directed toward God, in a setting where others happened to be present. He was not performing for the crowd.

But there is a real principle here. At some point, faith becomes visible or it withers. Baptism is visible. Gathering with God's people is visible. Generosity is visible. Forgiving someone who wronged you is visible.

Jesus said, Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven (Mtt 5:16). Notice where the glory lands — on the Father, not on the person.

Private devotion feeds public faithfulness. Public faithfulness proves private devotion was real.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my faith visible in any way to the people around me?
2. When my faith does become visible, whose glory is it serving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let my faith be real enough to be seen, and humble enough that people see You in it rather than me. Amen.
